item.title: [EN|In-Depth] BBC Global News Podcast (Tue 22:00): Special episode: Trump, Putin and Xi meeting
item.description:
Originally published Tue 17 Nov 2026 22:00 IST.

This special episode of the Global News Podcast brings together our China specialist, our North America correspondent, and our Russia and Ukraine analyst, to discuss an unprecedented summit taking place this week. The US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping are due to meet in Shenzhen, China, for their first-ever trilateral talks. President Trump has said the agenda will include denuclearisation, the war with Iran, and the war in Ukraine. So what could emerge from this meeting? Some analysts are hopeful that China could exert some influence on Tehran, and act as a mediator between Moscow and Kyiv. But Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said he's worried that the three leaders could try to reshape the international order as they see fit, without consulting smaller countries. Trump, Putin and Xi are also expected to talk about the economy and AI, particularly after Jensen Huang was ousted as CEO of Nvidia, following allegations that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. But will any big decisions come out of the talks in Shenzhen? Or is this about symbolism: a way for the leaders of China, the US and Russia to give themselves a boost and a distraction from their problems at home?
